summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR1,890 crore, with new vehicle volumes up about 81% reported and about 91% like-to-like. Reported EBITDA rose about 87% to INR71.5 crore, margin 3.8% vs 2.9%, helped by a one-off ~INR5 crore lease-modification gain in other income. Organic revenue grew 33% YoY, indicating the existing network contributed alongside the FY26 acquisitions (RKS Maruti, Globe CV BharatBenz, Audi/Olympus). Management said the acquired businesses are now EBITDA-positive in aggregate (~INR9.4 crore) but still loss-making below EBITDA due to depreciation and finance costs; reported PAT was INR1.4 crore vs a loss of INR8.8 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (ex-luxury)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR836 crore (+73% YoY reported, +54% excluding luxury per call); new vehicles 10,475 units (+83%); service volumes 1,90,801 (-5%) while service income INR169 crore (+11%). Organic PV revenue +49%. PV EBITDA margin ~4% per management, with Maruti ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at segment level.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR564 crore (+33% reported, +35% per call; organic +21%); new vehicles 3,495 units (+41%); service volumes 52,647 (+15%), service income INR107 crore (+47%). Sequentially volumes moderated vs Q4. Management cites CV EBITDA ~3.6-3.75%.

segments.name: EV (Ather two-wheelers and e-VITARA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore (+122% YoY; reported EV revenue +113%); new vehicles 3,330 units (+153%); service volumes 13,232 (+60%), service income ~INR3 crore. EBITDA ~INR2 crore; margin ~3.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects acquired businesses to be PAT-positive from Q2 FY27 onwards; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end of Q3, with Olympus possibly one more quarter.
RKS service volumes expected on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume growth expected at ~6-7% from Q2 (not the 15% previously guided), with ASP continuing to rise; Maruti service volumes expected to reach double digit from Q2.
Blended EBITDA margin: management hopes to reach ~4% and says ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% unlikely this year unless mix changes.
FY27 revenue targeted at INR8,200-8,300 crore vs ~INR6,400 crore in FY26 (~20-25% growth).
H2 PV growth so far running ~80-90% YoY in most months, expected to moderate on high base; Q3 flagged as key with Audi launch.
Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition or expansion planned; surplus cash to be used first for debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Q1 network additions: new Maruti Suzuki service centre at Koyilandy (Kerala), two Tata CV outlets at Perumbavoor and Kazhakuttam, and a JLR sales and service facility in Nagpur.
New vehicle inventory ~32 days vs ~50 days a year ago; absolute inventory up only ~14% YoY despite higher revenue; sequential build ahead of festive season and OEM launches.
Audi inventory elevated, expected to fall to ~20-25 days in August-September.
Ather inventory ~5 days, JLR supply somewhat constrained.
Keralam revenue share fell below 50% for the first time (49%), state mix: Tamil Nadu 22%, Karnataka 12%, Telangana 8%, Maharashtra 5%, Punjab 4%, Andhra Pradesh 0.3%.
demand_pricing: Pre-festive inquiries up ~20% YoY over recent days, ~17-18% over the last month; bookings up ~22% YoY.
Keralam inauspicious period ends 16 August; retail expected to pick up from 17 August (Onam-Chingam).
CV demand weak in construction: tipper segment low to negative growth; SCV and cargo holding.
Maruti price increases modest (INR5,000-7,000 for most models; INR10,000-15,000 for some), with no major impact on demand or margin.
Entry-level cars recovered: Alto K10 and WagonR strong; S-Presso slowing; Arena returned to growth.
Spare parts short supply in the market, causing vehicles to stay in workshops.
Running repairs up ~8.8% in July; free service turned to growth in Q1.
Commercial ticket size ~INR16-17 lakh is pulling blended margin down.

qa_highlights.question: How are inquiries and bookings trending into the festive period, and what is the H2 FY27 growth outlook for PV, CV and EV?
qa_highlights.answer: Inquiries up about 20% YoY over recent days and 17-18% over the last month; bookings up about 22% YoY. Keralam is in an inauspicious period until 16 August, with retail expected to pick up from 17 August. PV H2 growth running about 80-90% YoY in most months, likely to moderate on high base; Q3 seen as key with Audi launch. CV construction demand weak (tipper low to negative), SCV and cargo holding.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin move toward 4-5%, and how will the acquisitions' turnaround affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5% will take a long time because CV mix is rising (average CV ticket ~INR16-17 lakh). Blended margin hoped to reach ~4% and ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% not expected unless mix changes considerably. Acquired businesses are EBITDA-positive in aggregate at ~INR9.4 crore; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end Q3, Olympus possibly one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the INR11.2 crore adjusted PBT vs INR1.9 crore reported PBT?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is acquisition effects: acquisitions contributed ~INR9.4 crore EBITDA (Globe ~INR2.1 crore, RKS ~INR7.4 crore, Olympus neutral), offset by ~INR12 crore depreciation and ~INR6.8 crore finance cost. At PBT, RKS was about negative INR5.3 crore and Olympus about negative INR4 crore; Globe roughly neutral.

qa_highlights.question: What are the segment margins, ex-acquisitions, for PV and Luxury?
qa_highlights.answer: JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA roughly nil, dragging luxury margin. PV EBITDA about 4% now, up from INR9.4 crore to about INR35 crore on Maruti, with Honda a negative INR4.2 crore in Q1. Maruti margin ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at the model level, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Service volume guidance: is the 10-12% growth target on track after PV service volumes fell 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer expects 15%; PV service volume growth guided at ~6-7% from Q2 as Honda base drops out. Maruti service volumes up ~8% YoY, expected to reach double digit from Q2. Service ASP up ~15% in PV; Maruti ASP INR6.6 lakh to 6.7 lakh and JLR INR1.07 crore to INR1.26 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is new vehicle sales business profitable after interest cost, and what is the split of the INR30 crore finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Maruti sales EBITDA ~1.7% (vs about -2% a year ago), ~0.85% after interest; JLR ~5%; TCV/BharatBenz ~3% with interest under 1%; Ather ~4.2% with negligible interest. Split of the ~INR30 crore finance cost was not given on the call; to be emailed to the analyst.

risks_watch: Acquired RKS (Telangana Maruti) and Olympus (Audi) must reach PAT breakeven by end Q3 FY27 (Olympus possibly one quarter later); RKS service volumes targeted on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume recovery to ~6-7% growth from Q2 (vs earlier 10-12%/15% guidance) and running repairs reaching growth in Q2; spare parts short supply keeping vehicles in workshops.
Blended EBITDA margin ~4.3-4.4% by year end is below the earlier ~5% guidance; CV mix (ticket ~INR16-17 lakh) is diluting margin.
Debt higher YoY from FY26 acquisitions; finance cost ~INR30 crore and below-EBITDA depreciation (~INR12 crore in Q1) continue to hold reported PBT near breakeven.
Audi inventory elevated (expected to fall to ~20-25 days in Aug-Sep) and Audi margin at nil until Q3 launches; JLR supply constrained and Ather inventory ~5 days.
CV construction demand weak (tipper low to negative); Keralam market sentiment tied to Onam-Chingam timing; leadership transition as CEO Raj Narayan departs after August 2026.
key_quotes: So we might not inch to 5% this year, though the focus is to build that up. We will be closer to about 4.3%, 4.4% this year at the end of it.
But in terms of volume, we are hoping to grow from Q2 onwards. July numbers have come in pretty strong in terms of growth. So we're hoping to maintain that.
The acquired businesses have now reached a much healthy operating level and are contributing positively at the EBITDA level.
Currently, the only kind of the Capex spend that we have is more in terms of the replacement Capex and the current projects that are in progress.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the acquisition turnaround, but cautious and explicitly lowering prior guidance on service volume growth (15% to 6-7%) and on the 5% EBITDA margin target (now ~4.3-4.4% by year end). Management was candid about mix drag from CVs and Audi, and deferred some detail (finance cost split) to follow-up.
